      <title>Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/24/fears-return-to-war-tigray-rebels-launch-offensive-against-ethiopian-army</link>
      <description><p>Fighting escalates after Tigrayan rebels form new coalition aimed at overthrowing Abiy Ahmed government</p><p>There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.</p><p>About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/26/ethiopias-military-to-begin-final-offensive-against-tigray-capital">a devastating war</a> between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/24/fears-return-to-war-tigray-rebels-launch-offensive-against-ethiopian-army">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Arrest of Shadrack Sibiya comes as country reels from cases of femicide and alleged police corruption and criminality</p><p>One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls.</p><p>Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday.       <title>Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/25/weather-tracker-hurricane-polo-baja-california-mexico</link>
      <description><p>Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters</p><p>Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength.</p><p>Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/25/weather-tracker-hurricane-polo-baja-california-mexico">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>New research finds 485 chemicals in US pesticide products linked to breast cancer</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/26/breast-cancer-us-pesticide-products</link>
      <description><p>Paper raises questions about safety of food and other products as early onset breast cancer rates surge worldwide</p><p>New research has identified at least 485 chemicals used in US pesticide products that are linked to breast cancer, raising questions about the safety of food and other products at a time when early onset breast cancer rates are <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2025/feb/24/breast-cancer-diagnoses-deaths-surge-worldwide-who">surging worldwide</a>.</p><p>The new <a href="https://pubs.acs.org/evhpaz/article/doi/10.1021/EHP.6c00022/5436094/Guiding-Risk-Reduction-for-Breast-Cancer-Relevant">peer-reviewed paper</a>, published in Environmental Health Perspectives, a top journal from the American Chemical Society, highlights what public health advocates say are a range of deficiencies in how US pesticides are regulated. The review includes active pesticide ingredients, but also hundreds of so-called “inert”, or inactive, ingredients that typically do not undergo a thorough safety review.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/26/breast-cancer-us-pesticide-products">Continue reading...</a></description>
